A0222.title: Targeted Inspection
A0222.definition: Rule-based targeted inspection of high-risk merchants, sites, or courier tasks to verify consistency between physical goods and system data.
A0222.description: Targeted inspection initiates manual or systematic verification against high-risk merchants, outlets, or courier pickup/delivery tasks based on risk scores, historical anomalies, and scenario characteristics. It checks whether physical items, weight, routing, and delivery confirmations align with system data. This measure addresses data distortion risks such as weight fraud, false routing, and splitting heavy goods into smaller parcels, following the governance path of 'data anomaly → targeted verification → closed-loop resolution'. It must be paired with evidence collection and appeal mechanisms to avoid penalizing compliant fulfillment.
A0222.limitation: Inspection coverage is inherently limited and depends on the quality of risk scoring and sample representativeness. High-frequency inspections can impair normal fulfillment efficiency and merchant experience, requiring a careful balance between sampling rate and the cost of false positives.

A0222-001.title: Trusted-Merchant Targeted Inspection
A0222-001.definition: Low-frequency targeted inspection of trusted-list merchants to verify fulfillment goods and declaration consistency.
A0222-001.description: Trusted merchants typically enjoy inspection exemption or fast-track benefits. Directed spot checks use low-frequency sampling to verify that trust is not abused, focusing on whether the actual goods, weight, and category declarations match the order. While safeguarding trusted merchants' fulfillment efficiency, this measure identifies behaviors such as false shipments, product switching, or declaration discrepancies carried out under the guise of trust credentials. The governance direction is 'trust admission + sampling review + trust downgrade.'
A0222-001.limitation: Low-frequency sampling has limited capture rate for single-instance violations and must be supplemented by reports and anomaly monitoring to trigger additional inspections. The feedback loop from inspection results to trust ratings must be closed.

A0222-002.title: Courier Targeted Inspection Task
A0222-002.definition: Dispatching targeted inspection tasks for high-risk courier pickup/delivery tasks to verify weight, route, and sign-off authenticity.
A0222-002.description: For high-risk express pickup and delivery tasks, targeted spot checks are dispatched based on task-level risk scores to verify weight, route, and delivery authenticity. Targeting risks such as weight fraud, false routing, and fake handovers, quality inspection or risk control personnel conduct on-site or system-based verification to check whether the billed weight, node trajectory, and delivery data match the declarations. This approach pushes spot checks down to the individual task level, enabling timely interception of data falsification during fulfillment. The governance direction is: task scoring → targeted dispatch → on-site verification → liability handling.
A0222-002.limitation: On-site spot checks incur high labor costs and depend on the accuracy of task risk scoring. For tasks involving cross-branch or cross-partner operations, coordination of verification permissions is required.
